metaDescription: UI/UX design course in Adobe XD and Figma: design web and mobile interfaces and build clickable prototypes, with a guided 12-week plan and certificate.
shortDescription: Learn to design clear, usable interfaces for websites and apps and turn them into clickable prototypes, first in Adobe XD and then in Figma.
description:
This UI/UX design course teaches you to design websites and apps that people find easy to use, from the first wireframe to a clickable prototype you can test with real users.

Every bank app, online store and government portal is a set of design decisions. When they are made well, people complete their task without thinking about it; when they are not, they give up. Companies in Nigeria and abroad hire designers who can make those decisions with care and explain them. You will learn the tools and the reasoning together, one project at a time.

## What the UI/UX design course covers

- **Getting started.** What UI and UX mean, how designers work with developers, and setting up your workspace.
- **Design tools and features.** Artboards, shapes, text, images, masks, repeat grids, layers and alignment, using Adobe XD.
- **Saving and exporting.** Cloud documents, sharing for review and exporting assets in the right formats for developers.
- **Components and collaboration.** Reusable components with states, overriding instances, design systems and working on files with others.
- **Your first web design.** Planning a page from content and research, then designing a full landing page with clear hierarchy.
- **Responsive design.** Designing for desktop, tablet and mobile, layout grids, touch targets and responsive resize.
- **Prototyping.** Linking screens, transitions, auto-animate, overlays, scrolling areas and micro-interactions, plus respecting users who prefer reduced motion.
- **User experience.** User research, personas, user flows, visual hierarchy, usability testing and accessibility.
- **Figma from the ground up.** Design principles, the Figma interface, frames and shape tools, the pen tool, colour, gradients, masks, typography and effects.
- **Figma for product teams.** Auto layout, layout grids, components and variants, comments, Dev Mode, exporting, plugins, the Figma Community and team libraries.
- **Final Figma project.** A landing page, its mobile version and a clean handoff to developers, plus an extra lesson on Figma prototyping.

## How the programme works

You follow a guided 12-week plan that sets weekly goals: a group of short video lessons, practice straight after each one and a quiz at the end of every chapter. Each quiz is drawn from the lessons you have just watched, and every answer comes with a short explanation, so a wrong answer teaches you something instead of just costing you marks. If your weeks are unpredictable you can learn at your own pace instead, though most learners finish sooner with the plan.

Quizzes test both tool skills and design thinking: when to use a component, how big a touch target should be, what a search box needs in each state. The projects give you finished screens and prototypes for your portfolio.

## Tools you will use

You learn in two tools, one after the other. The first half of the plan uses Adobe XD to teach the core ideas of interface design. The second half moves to Figma, which is free to start and is the tool most product teams use today. Because you meet each idea twice, you learn what stays the same between tools and what changes: artboards become frames, components gain variants and prototyping gets smart animate. A laptop or desktop is needed for design work.

## Who it is for

The programme suits graphic designers moving into digital products, developers who want to design better interfaces, product and marketing staff who brief designers, and graduates looking for a creative tech career. You do not need drawing skills or any design experience to begin.

## After you finish

You will be able to research a user’s needs, plan a flow, design responsive screens with reusable components and build a prototype that others can click through and test. You will also understand how to hand designs over to developers cleanly, which is a large part of working well in a product team.

## Certificate and final exam

When you are ready, you can get your SkillsAir certificate. Once it is unlocked, you sit a timed final exam drawn from every chapter of the programme. Pass it and your certificate is issued with a verification link that employers and clients can check. Certified graduates can also apply for internship openings from our growing partner network, with no job guarantees.

Every learner also gets the free Freelancer’s Academy bonus course, which shows you how to set up a professional Fiverr profile and gigs so you can start finding paying clients for your new skills.

faq.question: Which design tool does the course use?
faq.answer: Both. You start in Adobe XD to learn the core ideas, then move to Figma for the second half, ending with a full Figma project. Figma is free to start.

faq.question: Do I need to be good at drawing?
faq.answer: No. Interface design depends on layout, hierarchy and understanding users far more than on drawing skills.

faq.question: Will I learn to code?
faq.answer: No. This programme focuses on design and prototyping. You will learn how to hand designs to developers, and you can pair it with our web development programme if you want to build them too.

faq.question: Will I have portfolio pieces?
faq.answer: Yes. You will design web landing pages in XD and Figma, a mobile version, responsive layouts and interactive prototypes you can show to employers and clients.

faq.question: Will I get a job after the course?
faq.answer: There are no job guarantees, but you will finish with practical skills and portfolio work. Certified graduates can apply for internship openings from our partner network.
